opening_move.text: Dell tells enterprises it's the best partner to bring them AI — we'd like to show your team what a customer types into dell.com search versus what they get back (376 results for 'lightweight business laptop with long battery life' — identical to a bare 'laptops' search).

hypotheses.title: Semantic / NLP search failure — qualifiers ignored, price constraints break recall
hypotheses.evidence: Returned 376 results — IDENTICAL to a bare 'laptops' search. Every qualifier (lightweight / business / long battery life) was ignored; the engine matched only the token 'laptop'. Separately, 'best laptop for gaming under $1500' collapsed to just 6 results — conversational syntax + the '$1500' price…
hypotheses.tied_to: Tested query: “lightweight business laptop with long battery life”
hypotheses.confidence_risk_note: Discovery-OS confidence×risk scoring is not yet stored for audit findings — surfaced un-ranked rather than inventing a score.

hypotheses.title: Blank empty state + broken no-results recovery
hypotheses.evidence: Empty search box shows nothing on focus — no popular, trending, or recent. Gibberish 'qwzxplmn' returned 4 spurious products instead of a clean empty state — worse than a good empty state because it shows irrelevant products under a nonsense query. No 'did you mean', no recovery affordance.
hypotheses.confidence_risk_note: Discovery-OS confidence×risk scoring is not yet stored for audit findings — surfaced un-ranked rather than inventing a score.

hypotheses.title: No search intelligence — zero analytics/behavioral signals in results
hypotheses.evidence: No Bestseller / Top-rated / Trending / Most-popular / New-arrival badges surfaced on any result cards (badge scan empty on laptops and desktop). Dell exposes zero behavioral or social-proof signal in the search UI, and the query stream is locked inside the home-grown engine.
